criteria.verdict_rule: FILL_PRICE_DOMINATES iff filling at the close recovers >= 60% of the one-bar gap (card - next_open); INFORMATION_DOMINATES iff it recovers < 25%; MIXED otherwise. Execution budget = the largest grid cost per side at which the close book still matches or beats the next-open book; NONE if even the no-extra-cost close book does not.

arms.card: same signal, filled at open[d] -- the published convention (not achievable)
arms.next_open: same signal shifted one bar, filled at open[d+1] -- the ledger convention
arms.close: same signal, filled and marked at close[d] -- closing auction (MOC)
arms.close_i<k>: close arm with k extra bp per side (auction impact + rank/fill gap)

criteria.frozen: thresholds written before the first run; --check refuses a face that does not reproduce them, and refuses a close arm that does not reproduce the look-ahead audit's own causal arm on the same panel

rows.what: fill at open[d] with the close[d] signal
same signal, fill at close[d] (closing auction)
same rule, one bar earlier, fill at open[d]
the executable ledger, no repo carry

verdict.rule: FILL_PRICE_DOMINATES iff filling at the close recovers >= 60% of the one-bar gap (card - next_open); INFORMATION_DOMINATES iff it recovers < 25%; MIXED otherwise. Execution budget = the largest grid cost per side at which the close book still matches or beats the next-open book; NONE if even the no-extra-cost close book does not.

notes: every arm holds the same names on the same grid; only the price series the book is filled and marked at changes (card/next_open: the open; close: the close)

the close arm ranks on the same close it trades -- institutionally that means the ordering is computed from last-tick data before the 14:57-15:00 auction, which is why the extra-cost grid exists instead of an assumption of free fills
the liquidity filter uses each bar's full-day turnover, which is only known at the close; that is inside the priced friction, not outside it
the toll is charged on turnover at the same 10bp/side in every arm, so a higher-turnover fill is not being flattered
